title: 10 Foods That Naturally Boost Your Immunity
excerpt: From citrus to mushrooms — discover the evidence-backed foods that keep your immune system strong all year round.
content:
Your immune system works around the clock, and the right foods give it the ammunition it needs. Here are the top 10 research-backed foods to include in your weekly diet.

1. Citrus Fruits

Vitamin C is famous for a reason — it supports the production of white blood cells. Include oranges, lemons, and grapefruit.

2. Garlic

Garlic's allicin content has been shown to reduce the severity of infections in several studies.

3. Ginger

A natural anti-inflammatory that helps soothe sore throats and supports digestion.

4. Spinach

Rich in vitamin C, beta-carotene and antioxidants — lightly cooked so the nutrients stay bioavailable.

5. Yogurt

Probiotics in yogurt feed healthy gut bacteria, where 70% of your immune system lives.

6. Almonds

Vitamin E is a fat-soluble antioxidant that protects cell membranes from damage.

7. Turmeric

Curcumin, turmeric's active compound, is a powerful anti-inflammatory and antioxidant.

8. Green Tea

Full of flavonoids and the amino acid L-theanine, which may support T-cell function.

9. Mushrooms

Beta-glucans in mushrooms modulate immune response — shiitake and maitake are excellent choices.

10. Papaya

Packed with vitamin C, folate and papain, an enzyme that aids digestion.

Remember: food is only half the story. Sleep, movement and stress management complete your immune picture.
author: Dr. Sushma Appaiah

title: The Complete PCOS-Friendly Diet Guide
excerpt: PCOS affects 1 in 10 women. Learn how strategic food choices can improve insulin sensitivity and balance your hormones.
content:
Polycystic Ovary Syndrome is largely an insulin-resistance disorder. That's good news — because it means nutrition has tremendous power to help.

Why Insulin Matters

When insulin levels run high, the ovaries produce more testosterone, worsening PCOS symptoms. Stabilising insulin is therefore the core of the PCOS diet.

What To Eat

  • High-fibre vegetables and legumes
  • Lean proteins at every meal
  • Healthy fats — nuts, seeds, avocado
  • Low-glycemic fruits in moderation

What To Limit

  • Refined sugar and white flour
  • Sugary beverages
  • Highly processed snacks

Timing Matters

Eating protein with every meal and avoiding long gaps between meals keeps blood sugar steady.

Supplements Worth Discussing

Inositol, omega-3 and vitamin D show meaningful benefits in PCOS research — always discuss with your nutritionist before starting.

Consistency beats perfection. Small, sustainable swaps create real change over time.
author: Dr. Sushma Appaiah

title: How To Lose Weight Without Losing Energy
excerpt: Crash diets leave you exhausted. Here's how to create a calorie deficit while keeping your energy, mood and muscle intact.
content:
Most diets fail because they ask you to eat less and suffer more. The science says otherwise — you can lose fat while feeling great.

1. Moderate, Not Extreme, Deficit

A 300–500 calorie deficit per day is enough to lose 0.5–1 kg weekly without crashing your metabolism.

2. Protein At Every Meal

Protein protects muscle, keeps you full and costs more energy to digest. Aim for 1.6–2.2 g per kg of body weight.

3. Don't Skip Carbs

Complex carbs fuel your brain and workouts. Focus on whole grains, fruits and vegetables.

4. Move Daily

NEAT — non-exercise activity like walking — burns more calories than most people realise.

5. Sleep Is Non-Negotiable

Sleep deprivation raises ghrelin and lowers leptin, driving hunger. Prioritise 7–8 hours.

Weight loss is a marathon, not a sprint. Build habits you can keep for life.
author: Dr. Sushma Appaiah

title: The Balanced Plate: Portion Control Made Simple
excerpt: No weighing scales required — the simple plate method helps you build balanced meals anywhere.
content:
Portion control doesn't need a kitchen scale. The plate method is visual, flexible and works for every cuisine.

Half The Plate: Vegetables

Fill half your plate with non-starchy vegetables — colour equals nutrients.

Quarter: Lean Protein

Chicken, fish, eggs, paneer, tofu or legumes — about the size of your palm.

Quarter: Whole Grains

Rice, roti, quinoa or millets — roughly a closed fist.

Don't Forget The Thumb

Healthy fats — oil, ghee, nuts — about a thumb's worth per meal.

Why It Works

The method naturally balances macros, controls calories and prevents the "clean plate club" trap.

Use the plate method for one week and watch your portions transform.
author: Dr. Sushma Appaiah

title: Diabetes And Diet: What Actually Works
excerpt: Blood-sugar friendly eating isn't about eliminating carbs — it's about choosing the right ones at the right time.
content:
Diabetes management through diet is often misunderstood. Let's separate fact from fad.

Carbs Aren't The Enemy

The type, amount and timing of carbohydrates matter far more than avoiding them entirely.

Choose Low-GI Staples

Switch white rice for brown rice or millets, white bread for whole grain, and add legumes to every meal — fibre slows sugar absorption.

The Order Of Eating

Research shows eating protein and vegetables before carbohydrates significantly blunts post-meal blood sugar spikes.

Portion Discipline

Consistent portion sizes at consistent times help stabilise daily glucose patterns.

What To Watch

  • Hidden sugars in sauces and packaged foods
  • Sweetened beverages — the worst offenders
  • "Diet" foods that spike glucose anyway

Pair your nutrition plan with regular monitoring and your doctor's guidance.
author: Dr. Sushma Appaiah

title: Eating Right During Pregnancy: A Trimester Guide
excerpt: From folate in the first trimester to iron and calcium later — here's how your nutrition needs evolve through pregnancy.
content:
Nutrition during pregnancy shapes both maternal health and foetal development. Here's what changes in each trimester.

First Trimester

Focus on folate (400–800 mcg), ginger for nausea, and small frequent meals. Your calorie needs barely change — quality matters more than quantity.

Second Trimester

Calorie needs rise by roughly 300 kcal. Prioritise iron (with vitamin C for absorption), calcium and protein-rich foods.

Third Trimester

Omega-3 DHA supports baby's brain development. Watch sodium for swelling, and eat fibre-rich foods to combat constipation.

Foods To Avoid

  • Raw or undercooked meat and eggs
  • Unpasteurised dairy
  • High-mercury fish
  • Excess caffeine (limit to 200 mg/day)

Every pregnancy is unique — always pair your plan with your obstetrician's guidance.
author: Dr. Sushma Appaiah
